Invisible, resizable lock zone — double-tap it to lock your phone instantly. Place it anywhere and resize freely. It can never read your screen.

1. Activate device admin once (big button on the main screen).

2. Tap “Add lock zone to home screen”, or long-press your home screen → Widgets → Quick Lock. Add it several times to create multiple lock zones.

3. The new zone shows a dashed outline. Long-press it to move it, and drag the dots to resize it. When it is where you want it, turn off “Show zone outline” — the zone becomes 100% transparent and the whole area is the tap target.

4. Double-tap the area to lock the phone. After the first tap the zone flashes very subtly (“armed — tap again”).

5. Extra triggers: the “Lock screen” Quick Settings tile, or long-press the app icon → “Lock screen”.

6. Want fingerprint unlock after locking? Turn on “Power-button lock” (Lock method). Device-admin locks always make Android ask for your PIN.

Quick Lock not in “Device admin apps”, or Activate does nothing?

1. Restricted settings (Android 13+, stricter on Android 15–17): apps installed from a browser or file manager are blocked from device admin until you allow it. Open App info (button on the setup card) → ⋮ menu (top-right) → “Allow restricted settings” → confirm with your fingerprint/PIN. Then tap Activate again.

2. Advanced Protection (Settings → Security & privacy → Advanced Protection): when ON it can block sideloaded apps from admin activation. Turn it off, activate Quick Lock, then turn it back on.

3. Fresh install: different builds are signed with different keys. Uninstall the old Quick Lock first, then install the new APK — otherwise you get “App not installed”.

4. Settings path on Pixel (Android 17): Settings → Security & privacy → More security & privacy → Device admin → Quick Lock.

5. Guaranteed fallback via PC (USB debugging on):
adb shell dpm set-active-admin --user current com.solerunner26.lockscreenwidget/com.solerunner26.lockscreenwidget.LockDeviceAdminReceiver
Verify with: adb shell dumpsys device_policy (look for “Enabled Device Admins”)

Quick Lock has no internet permission, so it can never check for updates itself — that is what keeps it private. Updates come through Obtainium, a free open-source updater, instead.
One-time setup: 1. Install Obtainium (github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium, or F-Droid). 2. In Obtainium tap Add app and paste: github.com/solerunner26/LockScreenWidget 3. Tap Install. Allow Obtainium to install unknown apps when asked.
From then on, every new build pushed to the repo shows up in Obtainium as an update (with a notification). Tap Update — it downloads the ~2 MB APK and installs it over this one. No uninstall, your settings and device admin stay as they are.
If Android says the app conflicts with an existing package, the installed copy was signed with an older key: deactivate device admin, uninstall Quick Lock once, then install through Obtainium.

Why this app is safe:

• It never reads your screen. The optional “power-button lock” uses Android’s accessibility system only for its “lock screen” action, and is configured so it CANNOT read the screen: no window content, no events. It stays off unless you turn it on.

• It has NO internet permission — it cannot send any data anywhere, ever.

• Device admin is granted with the “force lock” policy only: the app can lock the screen and do nothing else (no wipe, no password changes, no camera/mic). Revoke it anytime here or under Settings → Security → Device admin apps.

• Zero battery impact: the widget reacts only to your taps (updatePeriodMillis = 0). No alarms, no boot receivers, no wake locks. The optional power-button lock is an idle service that receives no events, so it uses no CPU.

• Every app screen is FLAG_SECURE — it cannot appear in screenshots or screen recordings.

• It collects, stores and shares no data. Settings live only on this device (private storage, excluded from backup/transfer).

• Widget taps carry a random per-install secret, so no other app can trigger a lock; all PendingIntents are immutable and every component is explicitly declared.
